A2-24.label: American Film Noir
A2-24.defn: A Hollywood crime film of the classical noir period (c.1940–1960), with its fatalistic, shadowed visual style and doomed protagonists, plus late-1930s American precursors (Double Indemnity, Out of the Past, The Asphalt Jungle, Touch of Evil). British noir and non-Anglophone noir of the same years are separate leaves; post-classical noir goes to A2-25.
A2-24.axis: Paul Schrader's phases of classic noir ("Notes on Film Noir", 1972)

new_leaves.label: British Noir
new_leaves.breadth: British crime films of the 1930s–early 1960s in the noir manner
new_leaves.defn: A British crime film of c.1929–1963 sharing film noir's fatalism and night-time urban style — spiv films, post-war crime melodramas and their quota-quickie precursors (Odd Man Out, The Third Man, Brighton Rock, It Always Rains on Sunday, Night and the City).

new_leaves.label: International Film Noir
new_leaves.breadth: classical-era noir and its precursors outside Hollywood and Britain
new_leaves.defn: A crime film of c.1913–1967 made outside the US and UK in the noir manner — French poetic-realist and policier precursors and contemporaries, Italian, Spanish and other European noir, Japanese and East Asian noir, and Mexican and Argentine cine negro (Le Corbeau, Touchez pas au grisbi, Drunken Angel, Pale Flower, Hardly a Criminal).
new_leaves.aliases: international noir; world noir; cine negro; film noir outside the United States
secs: Italian, German, Spanish & Other European Noir

A16-19.defn: A drama of ordinary poor people shown in their material conditions — poverty, unemployment, precarity, the street and the slum (Rosetta, I, Daniel Blake, Salaam Bombay!, Accattone). Films centred on work and labour struggle go to Labour Film; peasant and village life to Rural Drama; a drama built around one named social issue goes to A16-22; Italian neorealism and kitchen-sink realism are movements with their own leaves.
A16-19.axis: by where the hardship falls (poverty and precarity, then the street and slum), each by era

new_leaves.label: Labour Film
new_leaves.breadth: realist dramas of work, the workplace, strikes and unions
new_leaves.defn: A realist drama whose subject is work itself — the factory, mine, dock, office or service job, the strike and the union, the dignity or exploitation of labour (Salt of the Earth, Norma Rae, The Working Class Goes to Heaven, Two Days, One Night, Sorry We Missed You).
new_leaves.aliases: labor film; workers' film; working-class film; strike film; proletarian film

new_leaves.label: Rural Drama
new_leaves.breadth: realist dramas of peasant, farming and village life
new_leaves.defn: A realist drama of peasants, farmers, fishers and herders and the hardship of village life on the land (The Grapes of Wrath, The Ballad of Narayama, The Story of Qiu Ju, Ixcanul, Happy as Lazzaro). The idealised German homeland film goes to Heimatfilm.
new_leaves.aliases: peasant film; village film; rural realism

A21-7.defn: A live-action fiction short whose engine is realist drama — social circumstance, childhood, relationships, crime or war — rather than comedy or genre (The Lunch Date, Wasp, The Present, Two Cars, One Night). Poetic, literary and auteurist shorts go to Art-House Short Film.
A21-7.axis: by the dramatic engine: social realism, childhood, relationships, crime, then war

new_leaves.label: Art-House Short Film
new_leaves.breadth: poetic, literary and auteurist fiction shorts
new_leaves.defn: A live-action fiction short made in the art-film manner — a literary adaptation, a poetic or formally experimental narrative, or a short by an established auteur (A Day in the Country, Pull My Daisy, Machorka-Muff, The Human Voice, The Wonderful Story of Henry Sugar).
new_leaves.aliases: art film short; auteur short; literary short film

A19-14.defn: A documentary portrait of one famous or public person — an entertainer, politician, activist, writer, thinker or scientist — other than a musician, artist, filmmaker or athlete (Won't You Be My Neighbor?, RBG, Joan Didion: The Center Will Not Hold, The Unknown Known). Portraits of private, unknown people go to Portrait Documentary; of a subculture or community to Subculture Documentary.
A19-14.axis: by the subject's public sphere: entertainment, public life, then letters and ideas

new_leaves.label: Portrait Documentary
new_leaves.breadth: documentary portraits of private, unknown or eccentric people
new_leaves.defn: A documentary portrait of a private person or a few ordinary people — an eccentric, an obsessive, a life at the margins, or a life followed over years — whose interest lies in the person, not their fame (Portrait of Jason, Gates of Heaven, American Movie, Grizzly Man, Stevie, the Up series).
new_leaves.aliases: documentary portrait; character documentary; portrait film

new_leaves.label: Subculture Documentary
new_leaves.breadth: documentaries portraying a subculture, scene or community of enthusiasts
new_leaves.defn: A documentary portrait of a group defined by a shared identity, scene or passion — drag and queer communities, youth and outlaw subcultures, hobbyists, fans and believers (Paris Is Burning, The Cockettes, Hell's Angels Forever, Wordplay, Indie Game: The Movie).

moves: unsolved murder of a nun; a true-crime investigation, not a portrait

A19-4.defn: A documentary that argues or meditates in a personal voice, usually through first-person narration over assembled images, here about images and cinema themselves, art and thought, or identity and the body (F for Fake, Histoire(s) du cinéma, Los Angeles Plays Itself, Tongues Untied, Blue). Essays on history and politics go to Political Essay Film; on place, cities and travel to Landscape Film; on the filmmaker's own life to A19-5.
A19-4.axis: by the essay's object: cinema and images, art and thought, then identity and the body
secs: Essays on Cinema & the Moving Image

new_leaves.label: Political Essay Film
new_leaves.breadth: essay films on history, politics and society
new_leaves.defn: An essay film whose object is history, politics or society, argued in a personal voice over assembled or found images — the militant essays of Marker and the Dziga Vertov Group, and their heirs in Farocki, Akomfrah, Curtis and Peck (A Grin Without a Cat, Ici et ailleurs, Handsworth Songs, Nostalgia for the Light, I Am Not Your Negro).
new_leaves.aliases: historical essay film; militant essay film; film-tract

new_leaves.label: Landscape Film
new_leaves.breadth: essay films about places, cities, landscapes and journeys
new_leaves.defn: An essay film that meditates on a place — a city, landscape, territory or journey — through observation and voice, including psychogeographic and travel essays (Sans Soleil, News from Home, London, My Winnipeg, Of Time and the City).
new_leaves.aliases: city essay; travel essay film; psychogeographic film

moves: performance portrait of Grace Jones, not an essay

A13-5.defn: A love story with no outside obstacle whose subject is the courtship of one couple: a chance encounter of a day or a night, a love traced over years, or love kept across distance (Before Sunrise, Past Lives, One Day, Like Crazy). A marriage in crisis or a breakup goes to Marriage Drama; love late in life or across a wide age gap to Late-Life & May–December Romance; an affair or triangle to A13-4.
A13-5.axis: by the span of the courtship shown: one encounter, years, distance

new_leaves.label: Marriage Drama
new_leaves.breadth: dramas of a marriage or long partnership, its crisis and breakup
new_leaves.defn: A drama of an established couple — a marriage or long partnership followed over time, its crisis, estrangement or breakup (Journey to Italy, Two for the Road, 5x2, Blue Valentine, Before Midnight, The Worst Person in the World).
new_leaves.aliases: marital drama; breakup film; divorce film

new_leaves.label: Late-Life & May–December Romance
new_leaves.breadth: love stories of old age or across a wide age gap
new_leaves.defn: A love story whose couple is elderly, or is separated by a wide difference in age (Away from Her, Our Souls at Night, Breezy, White Palace, Elegy).
new_leaves.aliases: May–December romance; autumn romance; age-gap romance
